style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: Clean isometric cutaway illustration, technical drawing style, axonometric projection. Asymmetric composition off-centre. A massive, towering expanse of densely packed, dark industrial storage racks dwarfing a tiny, brightly lit modular picking bay in the corner. Flat muted palette with one vivid amber accent colour on the small active bay. Thin consistent line weight, laid over a real weathered concrete plant floor. Recognisable hardware with racks, pallets, and trays showing visible depth. One directional light casting long shadows across the concrete, unlabelled, generous empty margin.
negative_prompt: text, typography, watermark, gibberish, lettering, labels, people, face, hands
rationale: An isometric cutaway perfectly visualizes the structural disparity of the warehouse footprint, demonstrating how much physical space and capital the 'long tail' consumes compared to the active work area.
subject: massive static storage racks dwarfing a small active picking bay
core_thesis: The long tail is not a margin problem — it is a floor-space and capital-days problem: score the prune on stock held per unit of work.
core_conflict: Positive gross margin vs. hidden floor-space and capital-days costs
